extracted.intended_audience: early-career biomedical researchers (assistant professors) and academic administrators seeking information about the Pew Scholars funding program
extracted.subtask_description: Information about who the Pew Scholars Program in the Biomedical Sciences supports and how the awards are made — specifically targeting early-career assistant professors doing biomedical research relevant to human health. Useful for potential applicants and institutional administrators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target population / candidate promise
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides funding to young investigators of outstanding promise in science relevant to the advancement of human health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program emphasizes candidates who are "young investigators of outstanding promise." (No additional selection/scoring details provided on this page.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Career-stage eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are individuals who are in their first few years of their appointment at the assistant professor level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program is explicitly aimed at investigators in the early phase of an assistant professorship; the page uses the phrase "first few years" to describe the intended appointment stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research focus / relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Science supported must be relevant to the advancement of human health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program scope is biomedical research with a clear connection to improving human health. The page does not list specific topic areas or exclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant recipient entity & purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The program makes grants to selected academic institutions to support the independent research of outstanding individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards are issued to institutions (not directly to individuals) with the stated purpose of supporting the scholar's independent research. No further administrative or budgetary requirements are described on this page.
